 Judgment
This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award passed by learned Senior Civil Judge & Addl.
Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal, Bailahongal (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC.No.831/2015 dated 01.12.2020
. This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, appellant is claiming enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
On 27.08.2014, at about 02.00 p.m. while appellant- claimant was proceeding towards his village Sunakumpi on a Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle bearing registration No.NXG KA-24/L-4871 and when he reached near Mekalamaradi cross and while he was crossing the Highway, at that time, the driver of NWKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-42/F-1071 came from the side of Yaragatti with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life and personal safety of others and dashed against the said motorcycle causing the accident.
Due to which, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.

Pursuant to the accident, claimant took treatment at Malaprabha Multi Specialty hospital, Bailahongal, as an inpatient for 12 days from 27.8.2014 to 7.9.2014 and he spent huge amount for his treatment during the period when he was inpatient.
Thereafter, claimant followed up the treatment.
4. It is the case of claimant that due to the occurrence of accident caused by negligent driving of the driver of NWKRTC bus, the claimant is partially disabled.
Due to which, he lost his earning capacity and he is unable to do any work, as he was doing prior to the occurrence of accident.

It is the case of claimant that prior to the occurrence of accident, the claimant was hale and healthy, aged about 44 years and was doing masonry work along with agriculture and earning a sum of Rs.13,000/- per month.

In view of the accident and the injuries sustained by the claimant and having incurred huge financial expenses for the treatment, the claimant preferred a claim petition seeking compensation against the respondent.

5. On service of notice, respondent who is the insurer of the offending vehicle filed detailed statement of objections and denied the claim made by the claimant inter alia denying, the age,
avocation, income and the medical expenses incurred by the claimant.

So also, the physical disability as claimed and alleged by the claimant due to the occurrence of accident, it is also pleaded Somayya S/O Basayya Pujer vs The Divisional Controller on 27 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126548468/
2 by the respondent that the accident was not caused due to the negligence of the driver of the bus, as he was cautiously driving the bus on the left side of the road, whereas the accident occurred due the negligence and rashness by the rider of the motorcycle, the claimant.

sentences.text: It is also pleaded that there were two vehicles involved in the occurrence of accident and the claim petition is devoid of merits and liable for dismissal on the ground of non joinder of necessary and proper parties.

Accordingly,
he sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and also examined the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P29.
On the other hand, respondent No.1-Insurer examined the conductor of the offending vehicle as RW.1 on their behalf.
However, no documents have been produced to substantiate the case.

8. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.3,75,000/- with interest @ 9% p.a. to the claimant.

Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
the claimant is before this Court challenging the impugned Judgment and Award.

9. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel appearing for the appellant-claimant that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is extremely on the lower side and it is liable to be enhanced for the reason that the Tribunal has not considered the correct income of the claimant and has ignored the material documents placed before the Court and also the fact that the claimant was employed as a mason as well as agriculture work and having produced Ex.P29, which is the RTC extract, the Tribunal has failed to take the same into consideration in awarding just and reasonable compensation.
Learned counsel further contended that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not taking appropriate income including the income prescribed in standard guidelines by the Legal Services Authority.

10. It is also the contention of learned counsel that the Tribunal has failed to take into consideration the evidence of Doctor (P.W-2), who has clearly stated on oath that implants were made for the fractures suffered by the claimant and no further medical expenses have been awarded by the Tribunal which is erroneous and the same requires to be granted in view of removal of implants due to the surgery conducted by the Doctor P.W.2.
11.

Learned counsel also contends that the compensation awarded under the other heads including pain and suffering, loss of income during laid up period, loss of amenities and enjoyment in life are all on the lower side and same require to be enhanced.
On this ground learned counsel seeks indulgence of this Court to allow the appeal and consequently enhance the compensation.

12. Per Contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurer vehemently contends that the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal is perfectly in order in accordance with the material evidence placed on record both oral and documentary and there is no scope of interference in the present matter as the Tribunal has considered the age, avocation and income of the claimant Somayya S/O Basayya Pujer vs The Divisional Controller on 27 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126548468/
3 and the gravity of the injuries suffered by the claimant while awarding compensation, which is just and reasonable and same does not call for interference by this Court.

sentences.text: Learned counsel further contends that the compensation awarded infact is on the higher side.
The interest also awarded is on the higher side to the extent of 9% per annum and same requires to be reduced.
On these grounds she seeks to dismiss the appeal preferred by the claimant.
13. Having heard the learned counsel for the claimant and learned counsel for respondent.

It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 27.08.2014 between the motorcycle ridden by the claimant and the Bus driven by the driver belonging to N.W.K.R.T.C. This fact is established by the claimant by producing of Ex.P.1 to 8.
These documents are produced by the claimant based on the enquiry and investigation conducted by the jurisdictional Police in the criminal case.
The said documents are not in serious dispute and same is not challenged by the driver of the Bus.
Nothing material has been placed before the Court to disprove the same.
The evidentiary value of Ex.P.1 to 8 are worthy of consideration on the basis of the records per-se and same cannot be ignored.
Moreover, in the case on hand there is no challenge made by the Insurance Company against the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the liability fixed by the Tribunal is not in serious challenge as no appeal is preferred by the Insurer.

In view of the same, the rashness and negligence attributed against the driver of the Bus is proved, this court would not want to delve into occurrence of accident, rashness and negligence and the liability attributed to the respondent, as the same is not disputed or questioned by any contra materials.
14. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income and the expenses met by the claimant, it is not in dispute that the claimant was aged 44 years, though he has claimed 42 years.
In this petition nothing material has been produced to prove the same.
However, in the Wound Certificate age is shown to be 42 years, accordingly the Tribunal has rightly accepted the age as 42 years.
Though the claimant has stated that he is a skilled worker and was earning income of Rs.13,000/- per month both mason and agricultural work.
Nothing material has been placed before the Court to prove the income drawn by the claimant.

In the absence of any material proof with regard to income, the Tribunal and this Court are left with no other alternative but to do guess work and same will have to be done in the standard manner for which the Legal Services Authority prescribes the notional income for the relevant year of accident.
The accident having occurred in the year 2014, the notional income chart prescribes Rs.7,500/- to be taken as monthly income where no evidence is placed by the claimant.
Under the circumstances, in the present case Rs.7,500/- per month is to be taken as income as against Rs.7,000/- per month assessed by the Tribunal.

15. The claimant has also got examined the Doctor as PW.2 who was deposed before the Court by stating that the claimant has sustained fracture of left intertrocanter femur and fracture of left radial neck and having surgically treated the claimant and fixed SA LT DHS on 29.08.2014 and fracture of IT femur left and A/K slab was applied.

The Doctor P.W.2 assessed that there was a disability of 45%
to the left lower limb and 15% to the left upper limb thereby assessing the total disability of 60% to the left upper limb -

sentences.text: and left lower limb, the Tribunal has taken the evidence of the expert into consideration and has rightly deducted 1/3rd of the total disability stated by the Doctor to assess the disability to the whole body to the extent of 20%.
I do not find any legal impediment and illegality or perversity in the order passed by the Tribunal in assessing the disability to the whole body and hence the same is not disturbed and retained.

16. The permanent disability suffered by the claimant to the extent of 20% will have to be taken into consideration while granting the loss of future income due to the disability, therefore, the loss of future earning is Rs.2,52,000/- (Income of Rs.7,500/- X 12 X 14 X 20%) as against Rs.2,35,200/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

17. In view of this Court enhancing the income from Rs.7,000/- per month to Rs.7,500/- per month and the claimant having sustained two fractures, it would not be possible for the claimant to immediately get back to work with the said two fractures and also requires follow up treatment, it is basic common sense that for a person to get back to his normal work and recuperate after sustaining two fractures to get back daily day to day activities.
- 11 - Therefore, the loss of income during laid up period comes to Rs.22,500/- (Rs.7,500/- X 3 months)
as against Rs.14,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
18. Towards pain and suffering, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-.
I do not find any illegality or infirmity in the same, hence, same is just and reasonable hence not interfered.
19. Towards medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- on the basis of medical bills and documents produced by the claimant.
There is no reason to interfere with the same.
Hence same is not disturbed.
20. Towards diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.12,000/.
It is not in dispute that the claimant was taken treatment as inpatient for a period of 12 days and accordingly Tribunal has awarded said amount.
There is no legal impediment or error in awarding the said amount and same is left intact.

21. Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment in life, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.14,000/- same requires interference and I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the claimant that it is on the lower side.
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head as against Rs.14,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: It is vehemently contended by the learned counsel for claimant that the Tribunal has grossly erred in not awarding compensation towards future medical expenses despite the fact that claimant has undergone surgery due to two fractures and implants have been made while conducting surgery on the claimant.
This fact is not in dispute.
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the claimant that some amount would have to be awarded for removal of implants.

Accordingly, I am of the opinion that Rs.10,000/- would be reasonable amount under this head.
23.
